Describe your task

Virtual assistant for real estate agents

A real estate virtual assistant helps agents, brokerages and property teams organise enquiries, viewings, listing changes and document deadlines.

A virtual assistant for realtors can check availability, confirm viewing times and make sure questions reach the right agent. After each enquiry, the property record shows the last contact, the next follow-up and who owns it.

During a sale or rental, we can track document deadlines and prepare approved listing updates. Your team reviews changes to public details and decides how to handle negotiations and exceptions.

Listings, transaction and property management support

A real estate virtual assistant can work across lead intake, listing launches, showings and transaction checklists within the brokerage’s instructions.

Listings and inside sales support

Combine enquiries from portals, email and social channels. Maintain buyer and seller records, apply approved qualification questions and follow-up scripts, and coordinate listing copy, photos, marketing, showings and open houses.

Contract-to-close coordination

A real estate virtual assistant can track milestones, collect agreed documents, schedule inspections and follow up on missing items. Keep pricing, contract terms and licensed advice with the agent.

Property management administration

Log tenant requests, maintenance visits, lease documents and renewal reminders. Maintain rent status and approved follow-ups while the property manager approves screening, terms and payments.

Book a viewing without losing the enquiry history

A virtual assistant for real estate agents can preserve the enquiry history. Your real estate virtual assistant should keep the prospect’s request beside the viewing details.

A prospect asks about a property through a listing portal and follows up by email. The viewing schedule is shared across several agents. A sample handoff links the enquiry, appointment and next action so the agent can spend time on the conversation itself.

  1. 01

    Match the enquiry to the property

    Check the listing reference and record the channel, contact preference and what the prospect asked. Look for an existing record before opening a new one. If the enquiry concerns a similar listing, confirm the address reference before using a template.

  2. 02

    Offer an approved viewing window

    Check the agent’s calendar and the property access instructions. Offer only the agreed windows and confirm who will attend. Record confirmation and route any access request that the real estate virtual assistant cannot verify under the normal rules.

  3. 03

    Prepare the agent’s follow-up

    Give the agent the confirmed time, property reference, source message and outstanding questions. After the viewing, note the outcome and schedule the agreed next action. Pass questions about terms or pricing directly to the agent.

Prepare the inputs and rules.

Your virtual assistant for realtors needs the current listing and calendar. Your real estate virtual assistant should check a routine booking before handling schedule exceptions.

Listing source of truth

Identify the approved source for availability, property details and images. Confirm which fields can be updated after approval and how a change should be recorded across portals.

Viewing rules

Give a calendar window, travel buffers and instructions for requests outside ordinary hours. Document who can provide access and which viewing changes require consent from another party.

Follow-up rules

Supply approved scripts and identify which channels may be used. Give an example of an ordinary reminder and an example of a question that belongs with a licensed agent.

Decide what happens when the normal rule fails.

Your real estate virtual assistant should flag a changed viewing slot. A virtual assistant for real estate agents needs confirmation before making a new commitment.

The portal and source sheet disagree

Record both values and ask the listing owner which is current. Hold the change until the owner approves the source data.

A viewing cannot go ahead

Use the approved cancellation route, explain the next available option and confirm the calendar update. Give the agent the previous appointment context so they can follow up.

A prospect asks about an offer

Log the request and contact information in the approved system. Route it to the agent with the source message and any deadline.

Check the work against the original brief.

Review your virtual assistant for realtors against the agreed appointment rules. Your real estate virtual assistant can identify enquiries still waiting for the agent.

Enquiry coverage

Check a sample of portal and email messages against the CRM. Look for missed records, duplicate enquiries and items without a named agent.

Viewing accuracy

Compare appointments with the confirmed time, attendees and access instructions. Review cancellations separately so they remain visible for follow-up.

Readiness for follow-up

Open a completed viewing record and ask whether the agent can tell what happened and what action is due without searching for another message.

Leave a record the next person can use.

A virtual assistant for real estate agents should leave confirmed slots and open requests together. Your real estate virtual assistant should include the next follow-up time.

Plan a virtual assistant for real estate agents

Plan your real estate virtual assistant around listing and viewing peaks. A virtual assistant for realtors needs a route for last-minute changes.

Real estate virtual assistant listing coverage

Prepare approved listing details and appointment windows before enquiries start. Log the property reference, enquiry source and requested viewing time together so an agent can check the full conversation before calling back.

Viewing windows

Define which slots can be offered and who can approve a late change. If an agent’s schedule shifts, keep a short list of affected appointments and the last update each prospect received.

After the event

Log attendance, follow-up commitments and any enquiries that still need a response. Route questions about offers, terms or screening to the responsible agent with the original question attached.

Frequently Asked Questions

Ask how your real estate virtual assistant handles incomplete enquiries. A virtual assistant for real estate agents should pass advice and negotiations to the responsible agent.

Can you update listings across several portals?

Start with the portals and fields in scope, the source for listing details, and who approves changes before publication.

Who responds when an enquiry turns into an offer?

The real estate virtual assistant can record the message and route it with context. The agent or broker owns negotiations, advice and commitments.

What can be prepared before a viewing?

Your real estate virtual assistant can check the approved property details, available slots and prospect’s request, then prepare a confirmation for the agreed review or sending process. Agents decide any exception to the scheduling rules.

Can the real estate virtual assistant keep our CRM records current?

A virtual assistant for realtors can log enquiry sources, contact details and agreed follow-up actions in the approved fields. Provide the rules for duplicates, ownership and which updates need an agent’s confirmation.

How are last-minute calendar conflicts handled?

Your virtual assistant for real estate agents should identify the affected appointments, record the latest information and ask the responsible agent to choose the next step. The agreed backup route should cover times when that agent is unavailable.

What do we need to provide during setup?

Bring current listing information, approved replies, viewing availability and a normal enquiry example. Confirm the workspace, the agent who approves changes and which questions should always be routed back before a commitment is made.
